taxonomic_note: Accepted as a species by major current authorities, but Texas native status is unresolved: POWO treats Texas as introduced while USDA GRIN and Flora of North America support native/southwestern-U.S. treatment.
look_here_first: E. DAVIDII vs E. DENTATA: Do NOT use leaf color, erect habit or leaf teeth alone. Examine the UNDERSIDE of a mature leaf: David's spurge generally has relatively SHORT, STIFF, STRONGLY TAPERED hairs, often arising from minute pustular bumps. Tooth-edged E. dentata generally has LONGER, WEAKER threadlike hairs. Then look at fully mature seed: David's spurge has a more ANGULAR cross section and irregular low bumps; E. dentata has smaller, ROUNDER, more evenly pebbled seeds. A fully mature capsule is generally about 4–4.8 mm wide in davidii vs 3.5–4 mm in dentata; measure with a real scale. Green three-lobed fruits and reddish leaves are shared clues, not proof. Without hairs or seed, report Euphorbia dentata–davidii group.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia: milky latex and cyathia; the dentata group is difficult enough that mature seed characters are often the safest species-level evidence.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual taprooted herb, typically erect to ascending; often more robust than E. dentata but habit overlaps.
morphology_keys.leaves: Mostly opposite, coarsely toothed, often more elliptic than E. dentata, but leaf shape overlaps too much to use alone.
morphology_keys.hairs: E. davidii shows noticeably shorter, stiffer, tapered hairs on the ABAXIAL (lower) blade, frequently with tiny enlarged bases. Under-leaf hairs are the first practical separating part from E. dentata, which has longer, slender flexible hairs.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Single yellow-green gland, broadly attached; opening oblong; appendages absent.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsules broadly ovoid, about 2.9–3.3 × 4–4.8 mm, 3-lobed and usually glabrous; larger than in E. dentata.
morphology_keys.seed: Dry mature seed 2.4–2.9 × 2.2–2.9 mm (FNA), angular cross section and irregularly clustered wartlike protuberances, contrasted with dentata smaller more rounded seed and more even fine bumps. Photograph at two rotational angles with 1 mm scale.
best_field_traits: Annual from taproot; tall or ascending, repeatedly branching, especially in disturbed open soil. Habit is variable and not species-specific.
Coarsely crenate-toothed leaves, frequently opposite, sometimes alternate higher in the plant; leaf blade shape and red/purple margin not reliable alone.
Some stems and leaf edges visibly hairy; key microscopic species feature is short, STIFF, strongly tapered hairs on the LEAF UNDERSIDE.
Short abaxial hair bases are often MINUTELY PUSTULAR; a second sharply focused macro is essential to truly see their bases.
Terminal small green cyathia and three-lobed fruiting capsules; one main yellow-green gland of oblong opening without petal-like appendages (must be a real macro to label).
Capsules glabrous or scarcely hairy, 2.9–3.3 mm high and 4–4.8 mm across in FNA. Need a scale; young fruits don't reliably match dimensions.
Mature seeds approximately 2.4–2.9 × 2.2–2.9 mm; angular in cross section with irregular/faintly transverse low wartlike bumps.
Confusion with E. dentata is documented in the botanical literature; seed sculpture and underside hairs are safer than plant height, red tinge or margins.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: E. davidii = stiff short hairs + larger capsule + larger angular irregularly lumpy seed. E. dentata = longer weak filiform hairs + smaller capsule + smaller rounded evenly finely tuberculate seed.
morphology_keys.family_genus: Family Euphorbiaceae, genus Euphorbia, section Poinsettia. Each little flower-like cyathium is a highly reduced INFLORESCENCE, not a five-petaled flower; its central female flower matures into a three-lobed capsule.
morphology_keys.family_lesson: Do not point to an entire cluster and call it 'a flower.' Each tiny cyathium is a flower-like unit holding extremely reduced flowers; distinct growing green tri-lobed fruits are capsules. Mature capsules may release seeds; photograph the actual released seed for comparisons.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Mostly opposite, often with alternate leaves on distal shoots, coarsely scalloped/dentate, often elliptic, and variable reddish coloration. Compare mature leaves; the same plant can have variable leaf outlines.
morphology_keys.capsule: Three-lobed capsule, approximately 2.9–3.3 × 4–4.8 mm, usually essentially glabrous. Only a mature intact fruit plus 1 mm ruler proves the width split against E. dentata.
morphology_keys.habitat_management: Occurs in open disturbed habitats, roadsides, streams, prairies and agricultural soil. Nativity in Texas is authority-conflicted (Kew introduced vs GRIN native); do not teach it as a confirmed Hays County native or automatically treat any plant as invasive without site-specific confirmation. White latex may irritate skin/eyes.
photo_steps: 1. Photograph whole plant and branches from one arm's length, including a mature crown and setting.
2. Record two mature leaves at an opposite node with a 1 mm/1 cm scale for petiole and toothed margin.
3. Turn a mature leaf over and take a SHARP underside hair close-up showing actual bases and whether stiff/tapered.
4. Photograph the cyathium separately from the swollen THREE-LOBED CAPSULE. Avoid labeling a green fruit a 'flower.'
5. Photograph mature intact capsule with mm scale (4–4.8 mm expected but may overlap).
6. Photograph one released SEED from front and side at 10–20× or stronger, with 1 mm ruler, to prove angular shape and uneven sculpturing.
7. If photo misses hairs and seed, report E. dentata–davidii group.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia davidii: shorter, stiffer, strongly tapered; often on minute pustular bases

comparisons.key_distinctions: Species-level pair E. davidii vs E. dentata: short stiff tapered underside hairs and angular, unevenly tuberculate mature seeds favor davidii; longer weak filiform hairs and smaller rounded, evenly fine-tuberculate seeds favor dentata. All green fruit and coarsely toothed leaf gallery views are group-level only. Cuphosperma is another regional toothed Euphorbia with hairier capsules, and red/pink showy bracts support cyathophora but are not diagnostic without gland anatomy.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: David's spurge: leaf underside & mature seed, not the red stem
steps: Begin at a branch tip: identify developing 3-lobed fruit and coarsely toothed leaves.
Now look at the actual E. davidii mature SEED photograph: the coat has coarse wartlike tubercles.
Compare the dentata leaf photo—coarse teeth are shared. The opposite species has smaller, more rounded, evenly finely pebbled seeds, but its matching public seed picture remains missing.
For a confident living field plant, examine underside leaf hairs (short/stiff/tapered for davidii, long/weak/threadlike for dentata).
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Toothed leaves + green 3-lobed capsules = E. dentata/davidii GROUP until underside hairs and/or fully mature seeds are documented.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The SeedImages photograph demonstrates authentic davidii seed bumps, not two-seed-species comparison or independent angular cross-sectional proof. The seed scale is present but divisions have not been independently calibrated. Stiff underside leaf hair bases remain missing.
